files.legend.sop:
@legend.space core.legend
    namespace=space
    version=0.1.0
    imports=core
    doc="Where things are: the projection a host world gives (items in a frame) and nothing else"

@space.frame core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="The frame the items are in: its width and height in the host's units, y grows downward. The optional step is how far one plain move goes (default a tenth of the width)."
    example="The drawing is 1000 wide and 700 high."

@space.frame.w core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="How wide is the frame?"

@space.frame.h core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="How high is the frame?"

@space.frame.step core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="How far is one step?"

@space.item core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="One object of the host as a box: its id, its kind, the centre (x, y), the size (w, h) and the stacking order (z). The module never sees more than this."
    example="The house is a box 120 wide and 120 high centred at 200, 400."

@space.item.id core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="Which object is it?"

@space.item.kind core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@space.item.x core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="Where is its centre across?"

@space.item.y core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="Where is its centre down?"

@space.item.w core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="How wide is it?"

@space.item.h core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="How high is it?"

@space.item.z core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="What is its stacking order?"

@space.item.shape core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What is its outline?"
    doc="Optional real outline: one or more polygons as offsets from the centre, written 'dx,dy dx,dy ...; dx,dy ...'. Overlap, non-overlap placement, tidy up and joining use this surface and fall back to the box."

@space.item.parts core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="Which boxes is it made of?"
    doc="Optional union of part boxes as offsets from the centre, written 'x,y,w,h; x,y,w,h'. Used as the surface when there is no shape."

@space.rule core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="A consistency rule every host gets after any spatial operation (generated from RULES in space.mjs by scripts/build-space-lexicon.mjs)."
    example="Everything stays inside the frame."

@space.rule.id core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Which rule is it?"

files.rules.sop:
@rule.space.inside_frame space.rule
    id=inside-frame
    doc="Everything stays inside the frame after any placement, move or layout."
    core.source="fixture:space/rules"

@rule.space.no_overlap space.rule
    id=no-overlap
    doc="After a placement or a layout nothing overlaps another thing by its real surface, unless the relation is containment (in, on, around) or the user asked for it."
    core.source="fixture:space/rules"

@rule.space.on_ground space.rule
    id=on-ground
    doc="A thing that stands on the ground (a house, a tree) is not lifted above the ground by a layout; a move that lifts it is done and said."
    core.source="fixture:space/rules"

@rule.space.face_limits space.rule
    id=face-limits
    doc="A slot of a face stays within its limits and keeps the order of a face: eyebrows above eyes above nose above mouth."
    core.source="fixture:space/rules"
files.world.sop:
@world.space core.world
    namespace=space
    version=0.1.0
    legend=$legend.space
    imports=world.core
    reasoner=matrix
    formalization=rules
    language=en
    status=fixture
    title="Space"
    summary=""
    doc="A shared module, not a tab: where things are, which one is meant by its position, how to move and arrange them. A host world (art.draw, diagram.sketch; later data.charts, geo.map, game boards) imports it and gives it a projection of its objects, space.item id kind x y w h z in a space.frame w h; the module answers with selections, boxes that do not overlap, layouts and answers about places, and the host applies them to its own objects. It has no patterns and no operations of its own, so it is never a routing target. The spatial words (left, right, above, between, middle, first, last, row, grid, a bit, all the way ...) are its lexicons. The rules and the arithmetic are in space.mjs, a browser-safe module the hosts import. Hand-built platform fixture, not produced by the C1 workflow."
